atoms.a: Aoraki / Mount Cook is New Zealand’s tallest mountain, rising over 3,700 metres on the country’s South Island.
atoms.sound: Aow-raki Mount Cook is New Zealand’s tallest mountain, rising over 3,700 metres on the country’s South Island.

atoms.a: Aoraki / Mount Cook is a sacred ancestral site for many Maori, New Zealand’s indigenous Polynesian people.
atoms.sound: Aow-raki Mount Cook is a sacred ancestral site for many Maori, New Zealand’s indigenous Polynesian people.

atoms.a: Its official name today combines both Maori culture and the colonial history of European settlers.
Next to this mountain, you can find the Tasman Glacier, New Zealand’s longest and largest.

hint.label: Glacier
hint.text: Glaciers are huge, slow-moving masses of ice.

trainers.instruction: Listen and select the correct statement.

b.sound: New Zealand’s national bird, the kiwi, is famously flightless.
Australia’s national bird, the kiwi, is famously flightless.
Without land mammals to prey on them for millions of years, many birds in New Zealand adapted to life on the ground.
Without land mammals to prey on them for millions of years, many birds in New Zealand adapted to life in the sea.
Humans later introduced land mammals to New Zealand, and today there are around 20 million more sheep than people!
Humans later introduced land mammals to New Zealand, and today there are around 20 million more lions than people!

atoms.b: Tonga is the only nation in Oceania that is still ((++ruled photographed)) by a king or queen from its indigenous people.
It is the only ((++Pacific Atlantic)) island nation that was never formally colonised by a foreign power, despite attempts by European settlers.

Members of the Tongan royal family often wear a traditional woven mat called a ta‘ovala around their ((++waists necks)). Worn by most Tongans during formal or festive occasions, it is a sign of respect and national identity.
atoms.sound: Members of the Tongan royal family often wear a traditional woven mat called a ta ovala around their waists. Worn by most Tongans during formal or festive occasions, it is a sign of respect and national identity.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Tattooing has been a Polynesian tradition for thousands of years. These tattoos typically represent parts of a person’s identity, such as family history or social status.
The word “tattoo” comes from the Tahitian tatau, which mimics the tapping sound of traditional tools. A small bone comb was dipped in ink and tapped into the skin to create the design.
atoms.sound: The word “tattoo” comes from the Tahitian “tatow”, which mimics the tapping sound of traditional tools. A small bone comb was dipped in ink and tapped into the skin to create the design.

atoms.text: New Zealand’s Maori have a sacred tattoo tradition called ta moko. These tattoos are often seen on the face and show a person’s ancestry and family connections, known as whakapapa.
atoms.sound: New Zealand’s Maori have a sacred tattoo tradition called ta moh-koh. These tattoos are often seen on the face and show a person’s ancestry and family connections, known as waka-papa.

atoms.a: What is typically represented by a Polynesian tattoo?
Where does the word “tattoo” come from?
In which country is ta moko a sacred tradition?
